x: Several of our "Juniors" ran well, including Button, Tom Pritchard, Davis, Field and others. A new member, Robertshaw, is promising and will do much better.

Looking through the list of sufferers, one sees such names as McMullen and Odell (Irish); Williams, Davis, Davies, Thomas and Powell (Welsh); Fletcher, Mitchell, Crighton, Stewart and McKay (Scotch); and Merlin (Cornish).

Several old timers were present including the brothers Spendlove, Bill Baker, Davis, of Ashcombe, Foster, and Alf Harley, of Belgrave. After the race the teams were entertained to tea by the Thames Hare and Hounds.
In the Long Jump, in Dick Negus again, Davis, Dorian and Geoffrey George we have potentially good performers, but all must do more to perfect their run-up.
100 Yards: 1 Negus (Bels.), 2 Sexton (W.M.S.), 3 Cook (Bels.). 220 Yards: 1 Sexton (W.M.S.), 2 Parker (Bels.), 3 Davis (W.M.S.). 440 Yards: 1 Betterton (Bels.), 2 Briggs (Bels.), 3 Burr (W.M.S.).
Included on the same programme were two Club Junior Handicaps, and with two heats in the 220 Yards the following qualified for the final : Sexton, A. Fleming, Freestone, Negus, Davis, and E.

Davis who also finished strongly, filled third place. The Junior mile followed and it was unfortunate that at the first bend, Stevens who had previously won the half, had the misfortune to fall and it was obvious that although he caught up with the runners, he had taken too much out of himself.

At 5 miles, Eric Hall, George Checkley, Davis of Woodford Green and Bob McMullen led the field with Beecham moving up. Harry was still hanging back, but catching sight of Fred Rolfe and Doub he put on pressure and soon passed them.

We were a bit disappointed to have been so near and yet not to have pulled it off but were cheered up a lot when we heard Bill had got a medal for second fastest time of the day (First fastest: Davis, Cranford School).

Tim Benjamin was the favourite in the 400 metres in spite of missing much pre-season conditioning, suffering a cold in the run up to the event and facing up to a Woodford Green onslaught in the form of Davis and Hedman.
